answer: An economy combats Sybil attacks by enforcing continuous synchronization over a rolling window of state updates. An adversary bears the cost of maintaining a distinct proof-of-stake state for each simulated node, creating a sequentially deep ridge of verification difficulty that scales with time; any attempt to spawn false nodes dissipates immediately as the epoch echo fades. Consequently, an attacker must maintain a constant chain of valid attestations to keep the protocol’s ember from burning out, effectively monetizing identity verification rather than cloning it.
